psalm noun

late Latin

Tert. Prax. 11 (Lewis & Short)
Vulg. Lc. 20.42

psalmus, psalmī m.

noun, second declension

Greek ψαλμός, a song to the strings (psallere, to play the cithara). The book is the psaltērium, the Psalter (Hier. Ep. 53.8, Lewis & Short). The Orthodox and the Latin psalter number the psalms as the Septuagint does, mostly one behind the Hebrew numbering of English Bibles: the Shepherd psalm is 22 in the Vulgate and 23 in the Hebrew.

Other words

  • psalma, psalmatis n.

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Aug. in Ps. 4 (Lewis & Short); Hier. Ep. 28 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • psalmīs et hymnīs cum ōrātis Deum, hoc versētur in corde quod prōfertur in vōce

    when you pray to God in psalms and hymns, let the heart turn over what the voice brings outAug. Reg. 2.3

  • et ipse David dīcit in librō Psalmōrum

    and David himself says in the book of PsalmsVulg. Lc. 20.42

See also hymn, Bible, chant.
